title: A contractor 'optimised' the network settings

form.title: Incident write-up — addressing brought back to standard
form.intro: Marcus has moved desks twice this month, which is exactly why the site bans fixed addresses. Record what you found and what you did about it.

fields.label: Reported symptom, in your own words
fields.placeholder: What did not work, and what still did.

fields.label: Root cause
fields.hint: Say where the address came from, and which setting made it so.

fields.label: What you changed
fields.hint: Which adapter, which setting, and what it is set to now.

fields.label: How you verified it
fields.hint: A machine with no route out still looks 'connected' — show the route.

briefing:
WORKSTATION-117 came back from an on-site visit with "hardcoded network
settings for speed". Nothing works now: no intranet, no shared drive, no web
browsing. The machine does answer to a remote session, which is how you are
connected to it.

The site standard is simple: workstations take their address from DHCP, on the
10.20.0.0/24 network, gateway 10.20.0.1. Warehouse machines are never given
fixed addresses because they get moved between desks.

Fix the machine's addressing so it matches the standard, and prove you have
working connectivity after the change.

objectives.text: The adapter takes its address from DHCP again
objectives.hint: `Get-NetIPInterface -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select InterfaceAlias, Dhcp` shows which adapters are static.
A wrong gateway is not a wrong address — the machine can look 'connected' with no route out.

objectives.text: The file server is reachable by name and port
objectives.hint: Fixing the address is not done until the service the user needs actually answers.

hints: `ipconfig /all` and `Get-NetIPAddress` show the address; `Get-NetRoute` shows whether a default route exists.
The contractor left a static address and a gateway of 10.20.0.254. DHCP would supply 10.20.0.1.
`Set-NetIPInterface -Dhcp Enabled` then `ipconfig /renew`, or set the adapter to 'Obtain an IP address automatically'.
reset_notes: Reset restores the static bogus address and gateway from the clean snapshot.

es.title: Un técnico externo «optimizó» la configuración de red
es.briefing:
WORKSTATION-117 volvió de una visita presencial con «direcciones fijas para más
velocidad». Ahora nada funciona: ni intranet, ni unidad compartida, ni navegación web.
La máquina responde a una sesión remota, que es como estás conectado a ella.

El estándar del sitio es simple: las estaciones toman su dirección por DHCP, en la red
10.20.0.0/24, con puerta de enlace 10.20.0.1. Las máquinas de almacén nunca reciben
direcciones fijas porque se mueven entre escritorios.

Corrige el direccionamiento de la máquina para que cumpla el estándar y demuestra que
tienes conectividad después del cambio.

objectives.dhcp-enabled: El adaptador vuelve a tomar su dirección por DHCP
objectives.gateway-reachable: La puerta de enlace predeterminada responde
objectives.reach-intranet: El servidor de archivos es accesible por nombre y puerto

hints: `ipconfig /all` y `Get-NetIPAddress` muestran la dirección; `Get-NetRoute` dice si existe una ruta predeterminada.
El técnico dejó una dirección estática y una puerta de enlace 10.20.0.254. DHCP entregaría 10.20.0.1.
`Set-NetIPInterface -Dhcp Enabled` y luego `ipconfig /renew`, o pon el adaptador en «Obtener una dirección IP automáticamente».
